design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (bank_deposit_transfers). Step 0 draw, printed by scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0: {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 4]}. Root bank_ext_recall_fee took 4 factors, prerequisite bank_ext_late_delivery_refund took 4. Task 1's draw (--tasks 2) is also 1 prerequisite / [4, 4].

WHY A GOOD TEST. A caller whose large house-deposit transfer went to a stranger's account because she transposed two CLABE digits asks only for the money back. The charter routes wrong details the customer supplied on a deposited transfer to a recall (bank_evt_recall: 'A recall and an error notice of wrong_account_details are mutually exclusive on one transfer: wrong details the customer supplied go to recall'), which is her own act with a fee she accepts. The recall rule says 'The recall fee is fixed only after the transfer's ledger carries any late-delivery refund owed on its transfer fee.' Nobody mentions lateness: the agent must notice from the records that the transfer was deposited 2026-09-15 after its date of availability 2026-09-11, read the on-time promise to see it is owed (the only hold was Paloma's own screening; no payout came back; no request-for-information answer on this transfer), work out a four-factor late-delivery refund, book it, and only then work out a four-factor recall fee whose service-recovery reduction reads that refund. Difficulty comes from reading two policies, three ledgers (bank, cash, account) and the hold history, never from picking among similar tools: each problem has exactly one tool.

SCOPE / SPACE BUDGET. Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed here: bank_ext_late_delivery_refund (refund_late_delivery_fee_f06ff624, agent) and bank_ext_recall_fee (request_transfer_recall_f96dc6b4, user). Left for task 1 (draw 1 prerequisite, factors [4, 4]): the whole error-resolution family (incorrect amount: Paloma's make-good credit, the customer's remedy choice), returns, cancellations, resends, re-quotes. Task 1 is planned on the incorrect-amount remedy (Paloma's make-good credit -> the customer's choice to have the shortfall delivered), disjoint from both policies and tools here.

POLICIES CLAIMED. (1) bank_ext_late_delivery_refund, trigger state_due (with no call at all, a late deposit on Paloma's side already owes the refund at month-end), subject [bank_fee_refunded], base_policy_refs = every base policy governing bank_fee_refunded: bank_evt_cancellation, bank_evt_error_resolution, bank_evt_on_time_promise. Overwrite: the base sentence 'Paloma refunds the transfer fee in full ... when the transfer was deposited after its date_available as last disclosed' is replaced (the amount is now the computed late-delivery refund; this retires the deposited_late gate, whose condition the new rule restates), and the base exclusion sentence about lateness 'from the customer: wrong beneficiary details the customer supplied' is replaced by a record test (a sender-attributed returned payout, or an RFI answer logged after the window). (2) bank_ext_recall_fee, trigger on_request, subject [bank_recall_requested, bank_fee_charged], base_policy_refs bank_evt_recall, bank_evt_pricing, bank_evt_amend_resend (all governing those events). Overwrite: 'recall_fee_usd is collected when the recall is requested, as fee_type recall_fee with the deposited payout's payout_attempt, and is not refunded whatever the outcome.' is replaced by the computed fee, still collected at request, against the recalled payout's attempt, never refunded. Inherited unchanged: deposited-only, recall window (60 days on Large Amount), one recall per transfer, no guarantee of recovery, recalled money handled as a sender-attributed return; the transfer fee refunded at most once; card fees outside the promise.

FACTOR CARD (verification run, handling-time worlds).
bank_ext_late_delivery_refund (result 8.79, fall-back 3.00):
- lateness_clock [method; evidence hold moment F(held_at), COUNT/LATEST of this transfer's RFI answers, DAYS]. Ladder: hold and no RFI answer -> calendar days booking date to deposit less delivery business days; hold and an RFI answer -> days from the latest answer less hold review and delivery business days; otherwise -> days from the date of availability. Tier taken: hold 2026-09-08T09:52:00 on record, no answer on this transfer -> 7 - 1 = 6. Baseline (from availability 2026-09-11) = 4 -> result 6.29. Near-miss: the RFI answer UPL-2506137734 on the customer's case file belongs to the earlier transfer PB-250610-21957; counting it would put the transfer on the answer tier.
- delay_share [parameter; days late]: >= 6 -> 70; 3-5 -> 45; otherwise 30. Tier taken 70. Baseline 30 -> 4.80.
- pickup_points [parameter; cross-difficulty cash; multi-source count AND total / count OR total]: >= 5 payouts and >= 1800.00 -> 15; otherwise >= 3 payouts or >= 1000.00 -> 8; else 0. Evidence cash_ledger cash_payout_made rows 2025-11-14, 2026-01-16, 2026-04-17, 2026-07-17 (4 payouts, 1600.00 within twelve whole months of 2026-09-18). Near-miss: the 2025-09-12 payout is 12 whole months back (MONTHS = 12, excluded); counting it gives 5 / 2000.00 and the high tier. Tier taken 8. Baseline 0 -> 7.99.
- principal_points [parameter; SUM bank_funds_received]: >= 5000 -> 10; 2000-4999.99 -> 5; else 0. Principal 8500.00 -> 10. Baseline 0 -> 7.79.
bank_ext_recall_fee (result 7.32, fall-back 15.00):
- recall_fee_basis [method; LATEST bank_payout_sent amount]: >= 25000 -> 0.12% of the payout instead of the listed fee (so the fee never drops across the 25000 band edge: 30.00 at 25000.00 against 29.99999 just below); 5000-24999.99 -> listed fee + 0.06% of the payout; otherwise listed fee. Payout 8500.00 -> 15.00 + 5.10 = 20.10. Baseline 15.00 -> 3.75.
- recall_standing_share [parameter; cross-difficulty account CPARAM level_number + MONTHS from CFIELD opened_date; multi-source]: Premier or above and >= 24 months -> 50; Verified Plus or Enhanced and >= 36 months -> 70; otherwise 100. Paloma Enhanced (4), opened 2019-04-02 = 89 months -> 70. Near-miss: level_effective_date 2024-01-15 (32 months) is not the tenure anchor. Baseline 100 -> 13.35.
- prompt_request_reduction [parameter; DAYS deposit -> handling]: <= 3 days -> 4.00; 4-10 -> 2.00; else 0. 3 days -> 4.00. Baseline 0 -> 11.32.
- service_recovery_reduction [parameter; COUNT late_delivery fee refunds AND DAYS availability -> deposit; multi-source]: refund on ledger and gap >= 3 -> 2.75; refund on ledger and gap 1-2 -> 1.25; else 0. After step 10: 1 refund, gap 4 -> 2.75. Baseline 0 -> 10.07.
No stamp decides any tier: the account's level is read with its opening date, lateness from dates and hold history, activity from ledger rows.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
Step 10 (bank_fee_refunded): bank_evt_cancellation.full_refund_window (time; anchor bank_transfers.booked_at, elapsed hours, inclusive 0.50 h) restricts only a fee refunded on cancellation; cancelled_at is empty, so it is satisfied vacuously; boundary cases recorded in temporal_feasibility (10:10:00 inside, 10:10:01 outside). bank_evt_cancellation.fee_refunded_once (dedup on related_entry_id): the 9.99 transfer-fee charge has no refund row at the opening. bank_evt_error_resolution: no gate on fee refunds (policy_scope); no notice exists. bank_evt_on_time_promise.deposited_late: retired by the declared overwrite, so the contract lists bank_evt_on_time_promise as policy_scope and cites the records the extended rule's restated lateness condition rests on (Large Amount on_time_promise true; deposit 2026-09-15 > availability 2026-09-11).
Step 12 (bank_recall_requested + bank_fee_charged): deposited_only (status deposited); recall_window (anchor bank_transfers.deposited_date 2026-09-15, 60 calendar days, inclusive: 2026-11-14 on time, 2026-11-15 late; 3 days elapsed); one_recall (the customer's only case row is an RFI answer on the other transfer; no recall request); bank_evt_pricing and bank_evt_amend_resend have no gate on this charge (policy_scope).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target: transfer PB-260908-24816 (bank_transfer_id bd3b0358-3921-49a7-bd86-8524d1256c3e). Correlation key for the refund: the transfer-fee charge entry e8823640-2438-4979-862e-9b29dc7e09e7; rows aggregated: its funds received 8500.00, fee 9.99, payout 8500.00 (attempt 1). Excluded: the 2025 transfer PB-250610-21957 with its three ledger rows and its RFI answer (different transfer id, different beneficiary account 012180004417265093, fully settled). The refund writes related_entry_id = the fee charge; the recall writes bank_transfer_id and payout_attempt 1.

WORLD ROWS AND WHY. customers/sender_accounts/recipients: identity, account level and tenure, saved CLABE 012180015834729361 (the typo, copied onto the transfer). bank_transfers x0: the object; its held_at, date_available, deposited_date drive the lateness clock, the delay share, both reductions. x0p + ledger + RFI case: the settled look-alike and the case-file near-miss; deleting the case row removes the near-miss, deleting x0p removes the excludable object. cash_transfers + cash_ledger (5 transfers, 15 rows): pickup points; deleting the four in-window payouts drops the points to 0 (refund 7.99). No base automatic clause fires: every cash and bank transfer is closed and settled, no hold is open, no notice is open, no rewards membership exists to earn points.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root bank_ext_recall_fee (user tool request_transfer_recall_f96dc6b4). One prerequisite: bank_ext_late_delivery_refund (agent tool refund_late_delivery_fee_f06ff624). Edge: kind value_input, gate compute binding late_refunds_booked, form state, prerequisite sentence (in the recall rule, affirmative direction, as a fee desk states it): 'The recall fee is fixed only after the transfer's ledger carries any late-delivery refund owed on its transfer fee.' Four-point test: ordering connective 'only after'; record-visible state (a late-delivery fee refund on the transfer's ledger); no tool, id or code token; strength 'only after', scope 'any ... owed' (open: zero refunds needed when none is owed). Exactly one write of this difficulty books a fee refund with reason late delivery: the late-delivery refund policy's tool. Derivation: sentence + ledger (no late-delivery refund, transfer deposited after availability) + the on-time rule ('a transfer deposited after its date of availability is owed a late-delivery refund ... booked as one refund against the transfer-fee charge with the reason late delivery') -> book that refund first. False at frozen_time: bank_ledger has only funds/fee/payout for x0, fees_held_usd 9.99. Flips: step 10 books 8.79, late_refunds_booked 0 -> 1. Topological order: late refund (step 10) then recall (step 12); single edge, no parallel branch. Deletion sensitivity (verification run): skipping step 10 -> recall_fee_usd 10.07 instead of 7.32. user_scenario never mentions lateness, the date of availability, the fee or any refund except as a reaction. Tools validate nothing (see tools_do_not_block).

LENGTH AND BREADTH. Surface goal (get the money back) -> recall policy -> its prerequisite sentence -> on-time policy (eligibility: tier promise, deposit after availability, lateness attribution by hold/return/RFI records) -> late-delivery refund (4 factors across bank ledger, case file, hold history, cash ledger) -> recall fee (4 factors across the payout, the account level and opening date, the deposit date, the new refund). Breadth: account category (level + tenure), cash category (payout history, 12-month window), two transfers to tell apart, the hold history.

EASY MISTAKES AND HOW A CAREFUL AGENT AVOIDS THEM. (a) Treating the wrong account as a reason to deny the on-time promise: the rule attributes lateness to the customer only on a sender-attributed returned payout or a late RFI answer; nothing came back here. (b) Counting lateness from the date of availability (4 days, share 45) instead of from the booking because a Paloma hold is on record (6 days, share 70). (c) Counting the RFI answer of the 2025 transfer. (d) Counting the 2025-09-12 Cash Pickup payout (12 whole months back) and taking 15 points. (e) Anchoring account tenure on the level date. (f) Charging the listed recall fee 15.00, or computing the recall fee before the refund (10.07). (g) Refunding the whole 9.99 transfer fee as the base promise used to say.

PERSONA DESIGN. Marisol speaks in full sentences with the receipt open; volunteers only the goal and the typo story (both grounded: the transfer carries CLABE 012180015834729361, the saved recipient too); identity items one or two at a time when asked (phone 7135550127, DOB 1986-03-14, ZIP 77036, email, ID 2M58); the correct CLABE only if asked; passive reactions: agrees when told part of the fee is owed back, accepts the recall fee the agent states without asking how it was computed, submits the recall herself only when it is handed over, closes once the request shows as submitted (the last gold action). She asks nothing outside the recall and makes no second request.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate by phone, verify with phone + DOB + ZIP; read transfers, saved recipients, bank ledger, bank cases, sender account, cash transfers and cash ledger; book the late-delivery refund 8.79 against fee entry e8823640-2438-4979-862e-9b29dc7e09e7; hand over the recall tool; the customer submits bank_transfer_id bd3b0358-3921-49a7-bd86-8524d1256c3e, payout_attempt 1, recall_fee_usd 7.32.

VERIFICATION CODE (authoring/verify.py, deleted after authoring; the gates re-run the same logic). It replays gold writes with the real tools to each step's handling time, evaluates the policy compute, substitutes each factor's baseline, all baselines, and skips the prerequisite write. Output: late refund result 8.79 (factors 6.29 / 4.80 / 7.99 / 7.79, all-baseline 3.00); recall fee result 7.32 (factors 3.75 / 13.35 / 11.32 / 10.07, all-baseline 15.00); skipping the late refund -> 10.07 with late_refunds_booked 0. Gates for --task 0: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

CLOSURE. policy -> tool -> computation -> GT -> terminal: bank_ext_late_delivery_refund -> refund_late_delivery_fee_f06ff624 -> computations[0] step 10 refund_amount_usd 8.79 -> fee refund row (late_delivery, related to the fee charge), fees_held 1.20; bank_ext_recall_fee -> request_transfer_recall_f96dc6b4 -> computations[1] step 12 recall_fee_usd 7.32 -> recall case (open) + recall_fee charge attempt 1, fees_held 8.52. charter_scope = required_documents = [late refund, recall fee]; task_tools in first-call order.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. Masking compute/expected: the KB recall text names the late-delivery prerequisite; the records show the late deposit and the screening hold; the on-time text gives the share ladder, the clock rule and the points; the share is 70 + 8 + 10 = 88 of 9.99 -> 8.79; the recall text gives 20.10 x 70% - 4.00 - 2.75 = 7.32. Same objects, same order, same numbers as gold.

REVISIONS. (1) check_compute: factor delay_share had no evidence binding -> moved days_from_availability into it -> COMPUTE OK. (2) replay: 13 seed rows outside the read closure -> reads switched to customer-wide ledger/cases, added find_recipients and find_cash_transfers, dropped the two unread rate-sheet rows; steps shifted 8->10, 10->12 everywhere (computations, gold_actions, temporal_feasibility, prior_step) -> REPLAY OK.

REWORK ROUND 2 (audit env_0030_money_transfer_service/audits/policy_task/bank_deposit_transfers; task 0 verdict PASS, no red item). Observations acted on: O-2 - the recall large-payout rate is now 0.12% of the payout (was 0.10%), removing the fee drop at the 25000 band edge; this world sits on the mid band, so the recall fee stays 7.32 and every figure in this dossier is unchanged. T0-O2 - the retired deposited_late gate is now declared as bank_evt_on_time_promise policy_scope with the record facts the restated rule rests on. T0-O3 - the persona's passive trigger no longer pre-describes the refund as partial ('owes you money back on the transfer fee'). O-5 - the late-delivery tool docstring says 'later than its promised date' instead of 'after'. Kept as recorded observations, no change: T0-O1 (the cancellation-window gate is listed satisfied because no cancellation exists: the gate restricts only refunds on cancellation, and the gate machinery requires the entry); O-1 (delay_share lists days_from_availability so that its bindings read a date span; the ladder reads days_late); O-6 (after a partial late-delivery refund the base sentence 'unless it was already refunded under the on-time promise' leaves the rest of the transfer fee outside a later error-resolution refund; no world of this difficulty combines the two). Re-run: verification 8.79 / 7.32 and skip-refund 10.07 unchanged; full gate block green.
user_scenario: You are Marisol Quintero Vega, a dental hygienist in Houston, Texas, calling Paloma Remit from your phone on a work break. You are worried but organised, you speak in full sentences and you keep the receipt open in the Paloma app while you talk. On September 8 you sent your younger brother Esteban Quintero Vega $8,500 through a Bank Deposit transfer to his BBVA México account in Guadalajara, the down payment for the house he is buying; the receipt shows confirmation number PB-260908-24816. Esteban opened a new BBVA account this summer and you typed his new CLABE into his saved recipient details yourself. Yesterday he told you the bank says nothing ever came into his account, and when you compared the receipt with the CLABE he had texted you, you saw that you had swapped the last two digits: the receipt says 012180015834729361 and his real CLABE is 012180015834729316. So the money went into somebody else's account because of your typo, and what you want today is for Paloma to try to get that money back from the account it went to. You open with that: the transfer to your brother went to the wrong account because you mistyped his account number, and you need Paloma to get it back. You do not know how Paloma handles this, or what it costs, and you do not guess. You give identifying details only when the agent asks for them, one or two at a time: your mobile number is 7135550127, your date of birth is 1986-03-14, your ZIP code is 77036, your email is mquintero.vega@gmail.com and the last four characters of your ID are 2M58. If the agent asks which transfer, you read out the confirmation number, the date you sent it and the amount. If the agent asks for Esteban's correct account number you read out 012180015834729316, but you understand that today is about getting the money back, and you do not ask for it to be sent anywhere else. You are not asked to decide anything else, and you do not ask for anything else. If the agent tells you that Paloma owes you money back on the transfer fee of this transfer, you are pleasantly surprised, say that is fine with you, and let the agent go ahead. When the agent explains that asking the beneficiary bank for the money back is a request you make yourself and tells you what it costs, you accept that fee, because getting the money back matters far more; you do not argue about the amount and you do not ask how it was worked out. Only when the agent says the request has been handed to you do you submit it yourself, with exactly the details the agent gives you, and then you read back what the app shows you. If the agent asks whether Paloma can guarantee the money comes back, or tells you it cannot, you say you understand it depends on the other bank. Once your recall request shows as submitted, you thank the agent and say goodbye.

request_alignment.claim: The customer asks Paloma to get back the money of her Bank Deposit transfer PB-260908-24816, which was credited to an account other than her brother's because she mistyped his account number.
evidence: user_scenario:what you want today is for Paloma to try to get that money back from the account it went to

gold_actions.business_effect: Paloma books a late-delivery refund of 8.79 against the 9.99 transfer-fee charge of PB-260908-24816, because the transfer was deposited on 2026-09-15 after its date of availability 2026-09-11 with the delay on Paloma's side (a screening hold, no request for information, no payout returned).

request_binding.action_semantics: A state-due obligation, not a customer request: under the on-time promise a transfer deposited after its date of availability for a reason on Paloma's side is owed a late-delivery refund on its transfer fee, and the recall fee the customer asks about is fixed only after that refund stands on the ledger. No other refund applies: there is no cancellation, no error notice, no return.

discriminator.business_meaning: a fee refund for late delivery against the transfer-fee charge, not a cancellation or error-resolution refund

stage_provenance.fact: The late-delivery refund is booked synchronously by this write; the lateness it rests on (deposit 2026-09-15 after availability 2026-09-11) is already on record at the opening.

base_preconditions.condition: A fee is refunded in full on cancellation only when the customer confirms the cancellation within cancel_full_refund_window_hours elapsed hours after the transfer was booked.
Each fee charge is refunded at most once.
Error resolution refunds fees on error_found; no error notice exists on this transfer, so it adds no gate to this late-delivery fee refund.

The on-time promise's only gate (deposited_late, 'Paloma refunds the transfer fee in full ... when the transfer was deposited after its date_available as last disclosed') is retired by the extended policy's declared overwrite; the extended rule restates the lateness condition, which the records meet: Large Amount carries the promise and the deposit 2026-09-15 came after the date of availability 2026-09-11.

gold_actions.business_effect: The customer opens a recall request on PB-260908-24816 and accepts the recall fee of 7.32, charged against payout attempt 1.

request_binding.action_semantics: The customer wants the money of a deposited transfer back from the account her own typo sent it to; the charter's route for wrong details the customer supplied on a deposited transfer is a recall (an error notice of wrong account details is for misrouting on Paloma's side, and a cancellation is impossible once deposited).

evidence: user_scenario:you need Paloma to get it back
user_scenario:you need Paloma to get it back

stage_provenance.fact: The late-delivery refund the recall fee waits on was booked by step 10; the deposit itself pre-exists at the opening.

base_preconditions.condition: A recall can be requested only on a transfer whose status is deposited.
A recall may be requested only within recall_window_days calendar days after the funds were deposited.
Only one recall may be requested per transfer.

Pricing fixes fees at booking and states that fees are never recalculated after booking except by a re-quote, a resend or a refund rule; the recall fee is a separate charge collected under the recall policy.
Amendment and resend fees apply to returned transfers; this deposited transfer has no return, so the resend rules add nothing to this fee charge.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A fee is refunded in full on cancellation only when the customer confirms the cancellation within cancel_full_refund_window_hours elapsed hours after the transfer was booked.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The window is measured in elapsed hours from booked_at to cancelled_at, and a cancellation at exactly the end of the window is inside it.

boundary_check.just_before: The clause restricts only a fee refunded on cancellation: a cancellation confirmed at 2026-09-08T10:10:00 (0.50 elapsed hours after the booking at 09:40:00) would refund every fee in full, one confirmed at 10:10:01 would not. This transfer was never cancelled (cancelled_at is empty), so the clause places no limit on the late-delivery refund and is satisfied vacuously.
boundary_check.at_boundary: At exactly 0.50 elapsed hours the cancellation is inside the window (inclusive boundary); irrelevant here because no cancellation exists and the refund's reason is late delivery.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A recall may be requested only within recall_window_days calendar days after the funds were deposited.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The window is counted in calendar days from deposited_date, and a request on deposited_date plus the window days is on time.

boundary_check.just_before: Deposited 2026-09-15; the Large Amount recall window is 60 calendar days, so a request on 2026-11-14 (deposit date plus 60 days) is still on time, and one on 2026-11-15 is late. At frozen_time 2026-09-18 only 3 days have passed.
boundary_check.at_boundary: A request dated 2026-11-14 is on time because the counting rule makes deposited_date plus the window days inclusive.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate Marisol Quintero Vega's customer profile from the mobile number she states, to obtain her customer reference number.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and both writes are keyed on the customer reference number; without it the identity check cannot run.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Verify the caller with three items she states (mobile number, date of birth, ZIP code) and record the pass.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must be verified before discussing or changing the customer's transfers; the recorded pass is scored state.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List her Bank Deposit transfers and single out the Large Amount transfer PB-260908-24816 she is calling about: its tier, status deposited, date of availability 2026-09-11, deposit date 2026-09-15, booking moment 2026-09-08T09:40:00 and the hold moment 2026-09-08T09:52:00 on record.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The recall gate (status deposited, recall window), the late-delivery eligibility (deposited after the date of availability) and the lateness clock, delay share, recall fee basis inputs, prompt-request reduction and service-recovery gap all read these fields; the older transfer PB-250610-21957 is the excludable look-alike.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her saved recipients: Esteban Quintero Vega's saved BBVA México CLABE is 012180015834729361, the number the transfer carried, while the customer's correct CLABE ends 316; Rosa Elena Vega Ruiz is the Cash Pickup recipient.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows the wrong account details came from the customer's own saved recipient, which makes a recall (not a wrong-account error notice) the route, and that no payout came back, so the delay is not the customer's lateness.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the money movements on her Bank Deposit transfers; for PB-260908-24816: principal collected 8500.00, the transfer-fee charge 9.99 (its entry reference) and the single payout of 8500.00 on attempt 1, with no late-delivery refund standing on it; the other three rows belong to the settled transfer PB-250610-21957.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Finds the unmet prerequisite of the recall fee (no late-delivery refund on the ledger), supplies the fee collected and the principal points of the late-delivery refund, the fee charge the refund points back to, and the payout amount and attempt the recall fee basis and the recall charge use.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her Bank Deposit case file: the only case is a request-for-information answer UPL-2506137734 logged in 2025 on the earlier transfer PB-250610-21957; PB-260908-24816 carries no logged answer, no recall request and no error notice.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The lateness clock picks the booking-date method only when a hold is on record and no request-for-information answer is logged on this transfer; the one-recall gate needs no earlier recall request; a wrong-account notice would exclude the recall.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her Personal Sender Account: level Paloma Enhanced, active, opened 2019-04-02 (level effective 2024-01-15).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The recall standing share is decided from the account level and the tenure counted from the opening date (not from the level date).

evaluation_criteria.objective: List her Cash Pickup transfers to her mother: five paid-out Cash Pickup Economy transfers of 400.00 between 2025-09 and 2026-07.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identifies which Cash Pickup transfers the payouts belong to and that they are paid out (not refunded or cancelled), the evidence the pickup points of the late-delivery refund rest on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her Cash Pickup money movements, in particular the five cash payouts of 400.00 dated 2025-09-12, 2025-11-14, 2026-01-16, 2026-04-17 and 2026-07-17.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The pickup points of the late-delivery refund are decided from the count and dollar total of Cash Pickup payouts in the last twelve months; the 2025-09-12 payout is the near-miss outside the window.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.refund_amount_usd: 8.79 = RND(9.99 transfer fee collected x 88 / 100). Share 88 = delay share 70 (lateness clock: hold on record, no request-for-information answer on this transfer's case file -> 7 calendar days from booking 2026-09-08 to deposit 2026-09-15 less 1 delivery business day = 6 >= long-delay count 6) + pickup points 8 (4 Cash Pickup payouts / 1600.00 in the last twelve months: mid tier) + principal points 10 (8500.00 >= 5000), under the full-share cap 100.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.bank_transfer_id: bd3b0358-3921-49a7-bd86-8524d1256c3e. Basis: the tool docstring asks for 'the reference number of the Bank Deposit transfer whose transfer fee is being refunded, as returned by the Bank Deposit transfer lookup'; find_bank_transfers returns this id for confirmation number PB-260908-24816, the transfer the customer quotes. Uniqueness: the only other transfer, PB-250610-21957, was deposited on its date of availability and is not the transfer whose fee is owed back.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.related_entry_id: e8823640-2438-4979-862e-9b29dc7e09e7. Basis: the late-delivery rule books 'one refund against the transfer-fee charge with the reason late delivery', and the docstring asks for 'the money movement that charged the transfer fee being refunded'. Uniqueness: find_bank_ledger for the transfer shows exactly one bank_fee_charged row with fee_type transfer_fee (9.99); the other rows are the funds received and the payout.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Hand the recall request tool over to the customer, since requesting the recall and accepting its fee are her own acts.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The recall is the customer's own decision under the recall policy; the hand-over has no DB effect and happens once.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The customer requests the recall of the 8500.00 payout and accepts the recall fee of 7.32 the agent explained, opening the recall request and charging the fee against payout attempt 1.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: bank_ext_recall_fee computes recall_fee_usd at this handling time, after the late-delivery refund landed; scoring unwraps to request_transfer_recall_f96dc6b4.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.recall_fee_usd: 7.32 = RND(MX(0, 20.10 x 70 / 100 - 4.00 - 2.75)). Fee basis 20.10 = listed Large Amount recall fee 15.00 + 0.06% of the 8500.00 payout (mid-payout band); standing share 70 (Paloma Enhanced, open 89 months since 2019-04-02); prompt-request reduction 4.00 (requested 3 days after the 2026-09-15 deposit); service-recovery reduction 2.75 (late-delivery refund now on the ledger, deposit 4 days after the 2026-09-11 date of availability).
argument_uniqueness_tracing.bank_transfer_id: bd3b0358-3921-49a7-bd86-8524d1256c3e. Basis: the docstring asks for 'the reference number of the Bank Deposit transfer to recall, as the support agent reads it out from the transfer record'; the agent reads it from find_bank_transfers for PB-260908-24816, the transfer the customer wants back. Uniqueness: it is the only deposited transfer whose beneficiary account 012180015834729361 differs from the CLABE the customer gives.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payout_attempt: 1. Basis: the recall rule books the fee 'against the attempt number of the payout being recalled', and 'The payout being recalled is the latest payout sent on the transfer'; find_bank_ledger shows a single bank_payout_sent row with payout_attempt 1. Uniqueness: there is no resend, so no other attempt exists.

factor_trace: lateness_clock (method): a hold moment 2026-09-08T09:52:00 is on record and the transfer's case file carries no logged request-for-information answer (the answer UPL-2506137734 belongs to the earlier transfer PB-250610-21957) -> tier 'hold, no answer': days late = DAYS(2026-09-08, 2026-09-15) 7 - delivery business days 1 = 6; the baseline counts from the date of availability 2026-09-11 and gives 4 days, which takes the mid-delay share and a refund of 6.29.
delay_share (parameter): 6 days late reaches the long-delay count 6 -> long-delay share 70; the baseline standard share 30 gives a refund of 4.80.

pickup_points (parameter, cross-difficulty cash, multi-source): Cash Pickup payouts within twelve whole months of 2026-09-18 are 2025-11-14, 2026-01-16, 2026-04-17 and 2026-07-17 = 4 payouts totalling 1600.00; not both high thresholds (5 and 1800) but at least the mid count 3 -> mid pickup points 8; the 2025-09-12 payout is exactly 12 whole months back and excluded (counting it would wrongly give 5 / 2000 and the high 15 points); the baseline (no points) gives 7.99.
principal_points (parameter): principal collected 8500.00 (bank_funds_received) is at or above the large-principal amount 5000 -> 10 points; the baseline (no points) gives 7.79.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: a hold was placed on the transfer and its case file carries no logged answer to a request for information
the days late reach the long-delay count
not both of those, but Cash Pickup payouts in the last twelve months number at least the mid pickup count or total at least the mid pickup amount
the principal collected on the transfer is at or above the large-principal amount

factor_trace: recall_fee_basis (method): the latest payout sent is 8500.00 (attempt 1, 2026-09-10), at or above the mid-payout floor 5000 and below the large-payout floor 25000 -> listed recall fee 15.00 + 0.06% of 8500.00 = 15.00 + 5.10 = 20.10; the baseline (listed fee alone) gives 3.75.

recall_standing_share (parameter, cross-difficulty account, multi-source): Personal Sender Account at Paloma Enhanced (level number 4, Verified Plus or Enhanced band) opened 2019-04-02 = 89 whole months >= standing tenure 36 -> standing share 70; counting tenure from the level date 2024-01-15 (32 months) would wrongly give the full share; the baseline full share gives 13.35.
prompt_request_reduction (parameter): deposited 2026-09-15, requested 2026-09-18 = 3 calendar days <= prompt-request window 3 -> 4.00 off; the baseline (no reduction) gives 11.32.

service_recovery_reduction (parameter): at handling time the ledger carries the late-delivery refund booked at step 10 (count 1) and the deposit came DAYS(2026-09-11, 2026-09-15) = 4 >= 3 days after the date of availability -> full 2.75 off; the baseline (no reduction) gives 10.07, as does skipping the prerequisite.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: the payout being recalled is at or above the mid-payout floor but below the large-payout floor
the Personal Sender Account is at Paloma Verified Plus or Paloma Enhanced and has been open for at least the standing tenure
the recall is requested no more than the prompt-request window of calendar days after the deposit date
the ledger carries a late-delivery refund and the deposit date came at least the service-recovery gap of calendar days after the date of availability

edges.condition: Whenever the transfer is owed a late-delivery refund under the on-time promise, a fee refund with the reason late delivery against its transfer-fee charge stands on the transfer's ledger.
edges.policy_source: The recall fee is fixed only after the transfer's ledger carries any late-delivery refund owed on its transfer fee.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The transfer is owed a late-delivery refund (Large Amount carries the on-time promise; deposited 2026-09-15 after the date of availability 2026-09-11; the only hold was Paloma's own screening, no request-for-information answer and no returned payout), yet its ledger holds only the funds received, the 9.99 transfer-fee charge and the payout: no fee refund with the reason late delivery exists, and the fees held still read 9.99.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The late-delivery refund write books one fee refund of 8.79 with reason late_delivery related to the transfer-fee charge, so the count of late-delivery refunds on the ledger becomes 1 and the fees held drop to 1.20; the recall fee's service-recovery reduction then becomes the full 2.75.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, no parallel prerequisites. The order is pinned by the recall policy's own prerequisite sentence ('The recall fee is fixed only after the transfer's ledger carries any late-delivery refund owed on its transfer fee.'): the late-delivery refund is written first (step 10), then the recall request with its fee (step 12). Reversing the two gives a different terminal state, because the recall fee then reads no late-delivery refund and comes to 10.07 instead of 7.32.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the late-delivery refund (verification run): late_refunds_booked 1 -> 0, recovery_reduction 2.75 -> 0, recall_fee_usd 7.32 -> 10.07; the terminal ledger also lacks the 8.79 late_delivery fee refund row and the transfer's fees_held_usd ends at 9.99 + 10.07 = 20.06 instead of 1.20 + 7.32 = 8.52.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona raises only the recall ('the transfer to your brother went to the wrong account because you mistyped his account number, and you need Paloma to get it back'). It never mentions the date of availability, lateness, the on-time promise, the transfer fee or any refund; it says she does not know how Paloma handles this or what it costs, and its only line about a fee refund is a passive reaction that fires after the agent says Paloma owes part of the fee back.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: request_transfer_recall_f96dc6b4 reads the transfer row only to copy customer_id and the held fees, then unconditionally creates the recall case and the recall_fee charge and updates fees_held_usd; it never inspects the ledger for a late-delivery refund, never raises and never returns an error. refund_late_delivery_fee_f06ff624 likewise books whatever amount it is given. An agent that skips the refund can still file the recall; only the terminal hash differs.
